title: DCR/CIMD refresh token deleted ~67 days after consent despite daily refreshes
answers: MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, v0) must re-authorize every ~67 days
refresh fails with invalid_grant even though client refreshes daily
OAuth refresh token deleted by cleanup job while still in use
body:
Symptom: Users of DCR/CIMD-registered MCP clients get `invalid_grant` on refresh about 67 days after first consent, even if they refresh every day.
Root cause: posthog/api/oauth/views.py `_save_bearer_token` (non-rotating branch) inserted a new access token per refresh but left OAuthRefreshToken.access_token linked to the authorization-code AT. The daily cleanup job (products/growth/dags/oauth.py) deletes an RT once its linked AT expired >60 days ago (AT lives 7 days => 67 days).
Fix pattern: In the same transaction/per-connection lock as the insert, repoint the RT's `access_token` FK to the newly created AT (`OAuthRefreshToken.objects.filter(pk=...).update(access_token=access_token)`), so RT lifetime tracks last refresh. Avoided a last-used column + migration.
Constraints: Applies to non-rotating refresh (DCR/CIMD). Rotating clients already create a new RT. Side effects: scopes for next refresh are read from the linked AT so narrowed scopes persist; the old AT stays valid until expiry and is then cleaned up as standalone.
applies: posthog/api/oauth/views.py non-rotating refresh path and the OAuth cleanup dag
